title: Transformations
description: Understanding reflection, rotation, translation, and enlargement of 2D shapes on a coordinate grid.

notes.heading: Reflection
notes.body: A mirror image across a mirror line. Each point is the same perpendicular distance from the mirror line as its image. Common mirror lines: x-axis, y-axis, y=x, or vertical/horizontal lines like x=2. The shape stays the same size and shape (congruent).

notes.heading: Rotation
notes.body: Turns a shape around a fixed centre of rotation. Describe with: (1) centre point, (2) angle (90°, 180°, 270°), (3) direction (clockwise/anticlockwise). Use tracing paper to rotate on a grid. The shape is congruent to the original — only orientation changes.

notes.heading: Translation
notes.body: Slides a shape without turning, flipping, or resizing. Described by a column vector: top number = horizontal (positive=right), bottom number = vertical (positive=up). Vector (3,−2) means move 3 right and 2 down. Every point moves by the same vector.

notes.heading: Enlargement
notes.body: Changes shape size by a scale factor about a centre of enlargement. Scale factor > 1 = bigger; between 0 and 1 = smaller. At Year 7, centre is usually (0,0): multiply each coordinate by the scale factor. The enlarged shape is similar (same shape, different size), not congruent.

notes.heading: ⚠️ Rotation direction
notes.body: A 90° clockwise rotation is the same as a 270° anticlockwise rotation. Use tracing paper or imagine turning the page. Always name the centre, angle and direction when describing a rotation.

notes.heading: ✅ Congruent vs similar
notes.body: Reflections, rotations and translations produce congruent shapes — same size and shape. Enlargements produce similar shapes — same shape but a different size. Check by comparing side lengths and angles.

questions.stem: Which transformation creates a mirror image?
questions.explanation: Reflection flips a shape across a mirror line.

questions.stem: Point (3,4) reflected in x-axis. New coordinates?
Point (2,−5) reflected in y-axis. New coordinates?
Square vertices (1,1),(3,1),(3,3),(1,3) enlarged by scale factor 2 around (0,0). New vertices?

questions.explanation: Only enlargement changes size. Others are congruent.
Distance from x=5 to x=1 is 4. Go 4 units other side: 1−4=−3. y stays 2.

questions.stem: A robot at point (4, 1) moves using translation vector (−3, 2). Where does it finish?
questions.explanation: Add the vector to the coordinates: x = 4 + (−3) = 1, y = 1 + 2 = 3. The robot finishes at (1, 3).

questions.stem: A shape is reflected in a vertical mirror line. Which coordinate changes?
questions.explanation: A vertical mirror line such as x = 0 (the y-axis) swaps the x-coordinate to its opposite but keeps the y-coordinate the same.

questions.stem: A triangle has vertices A(1,1), B(3,1), C(1,4). It is reflected in the y-axis, then the resulting image is reflected in the x-axis. What are the final coordinates of A?
questions.explanation: Reflect A(1,1) in the y-axis → (−1,1). Then reflect (−1,1) in the x-axis → (−1,−1). So the final coordinates of A are (−1, −1).
